title: Return GET request metadata
statement: The system shall respond to GET /get with a JSON object containing the request's URL, headers, arguments, and origin IP.
expected_outcomes: JSON body with keys url, args, headers, origin
error_pathways: HTTP 405 if a non-GET method is used

title: Reflect query parameters on GET
statement: The system shall include client-supplied query parameters under the 'args' key of the GET /get response body.
expected_outcomes: response args field mirrors query string

title: Reject non-GET on /get
statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 405 Method Not Allowed for any non-GET request to /get.

title: Return POST request metadata
statement: The system shall respond to POST /post with JSON including url, args, headers, form, data, files, json and origin.

title: Reject wrong method on /post
statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 405 for methods other than POST on /post.

title: Return PUT request metadata
statement: The system shall respond to PUT /put with JSON including url, args, headers, form, data, files, json and origin.

title: Reject wrong method on /put
statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 405 for methods other than PUT on /put.

title: Return PATCH request metadata
statement: The system shall respond to PATCH /patch with JSON including url, args, headers, form, data, files, json and origin.

title: Reject wrong method on /patch
statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 405 for methods other than PATCH on /patch.

title: Return DELETE request metadata
statement: The system shall respond to DELETE /delete with JSON including url, args, headers, form, data, files, json and origin.

title: Reject wrong method on /delete
statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 405 for methods other than DELETE on /delete.

title: Echo request headers
statement: The system shall respond to GET /headers with a JSON object whose 'headers' field mirrors the request headers received.

title: Hide environment headers by default
statement: The system shall omit environment-controlled internal headers (X-*-Env prefix) from /headers unless show_env=1 is set.

title: Return arbitrary status code
statement: The system shall respond to GET /status/<code> with an HTTP response bearing the requested status code, for codes 100 through 599.

title: Reject invalid status code
statement: The system shall return HTTP 400 when the status code path segment is not a valid integer.

title: Accept comma-separated status codes
statement: The system shall select one code at random when /status/<code> is called with a comma-separated list.

title: Support all HTTP verbs on /status/<code>
statement: The system shall accept GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD, OPTIONS, and TRACE on /status/<code>.

title: Basic-auth accepts correct credentials
statement: The system shall respond to GET /basic-auth/<user>/<passwd> with HTTP 200 and an authenticated=true JSON body when the supplied Basic credentials match.

title: Basic-auth rejects wrong password
statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 401 and WWW-Authenticate: Basic when Basic-auth credentials are missing or wrong.

title: Basic-auth rejects missing header
statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 401 when the Authorization header is entirely absent from a request to /basic-auth/<user>/<passwd>.

title: Chain N redirects
statement: The system shall redirect the client N times when GET /redirect/<n> is called, ending at /get on the final hop.

title: Redirect once when n==1
statement: The system shall respond with a single 302 to /get when /redirect/1 is called.

title: Reject non-positive redirect count
statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 400 when the redirect count is zero or negative.

title: Redirect to arbitrary URL
statement: The system shall issue an HTTP 302 redirect to the URL given by the 'url' query parameter of /redirect-to.

title: Redirect-to supports custom status codes
statement: The system shall honour the 'status_code' query parameter on /redirect-to for values 301, 302, 303, 307, and 308.

title: Redirect-to rejects invalid status code
statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 400 when /redirect-to receives a status_code outside the 300-399 range.

title: Redirect-to rejects invalid URL
statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 400 when the 'url' parameter of /redirect-to is missing or malformed.

title: Redirect-to accepts POST as well
statement: The system shall accept POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH, and TRACE on /redirect-to.

title: List cookies
statement: The system shall respond to GET /cookies with a JSON body listing all cookies present on the request.

title: Set cookie via path
statement: The system shall set a cookie of name=<name>, value=<value> and redirect to /cookies when GET /cookies/set/<name>/<value> is called.

title: Set cookie via query string
statement: The system shall set cookies for every k=v pair supplied in the query string of GET /cookies/set.

title: Delete cookie via query string
statement: The system shall expire cookies named in the query string of GET /cookies/delete and redirect to /cookies.

title: Cookies domain restriction
statement: The system shall not include cookies whose Domain attribute excludes the request host when responding to /cookies.

title: Include origin IP in echoed metadata
statement: The system shall include the client origin (X-Forwarded-For if present, else remote_addr) in the 'origin' field of all echo endpoints.
triggers: include origin ip in echoed metadata

title: Return JSON content type
statement: The system shall return application/json content type for all echo endpoints.

title: Return 404 for unknown routes
statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 404 for any path not matching a defined route.

title: Honour Accept: application/json
statement: The system shall respect an Accept: application/json request header by serialising responses as JSON.

title: Emit CORS Access-Control-Allow-Origin header
statement: The system shall include Access-Control-Allow-Origin=* on all responses to enable browser access.

title: Handle CORS pre-flight OPTIONS
statement: The system shall respond to OPTIONS requests with appropriate Access-Control-Allow-Methods and Access-Control-Allow-Headers.

title: Sequence header order preservation
statement: The system shall preserve the client-supplied order of duplicate headers in the /headers echo response.

title: Basic-auth handles special characters
statement: The system shall URL-decode <user> and <passwd> path segments before comparing against the supplied Basic credentials.

title: Redirect preserves relative or absolute style
statement: The system shall emit relative URLs on /redirect/<n> and absolute URLs on /absolute-redirect/<n>.
triggers: redirect preserves relative or absolute style

title: Include Content-Length on echo responses
statement: The system shall include a Content-Length header equal to the response body byte length on echo endpoints.

title: Cookie name path segment escaping
statement: The system shall percent-decode the <name> and <value> path segments in /cookies/set/<name>/<value>.

title: Status code sentence body
statement: The system shall include the standard reason phrase in the body when responding to /status/<code> with a code between 400 and 599.

title: /status/<code> accepts POST
statement: The system shall accept POST requests on /status/<code> and return the requested code.

title: Cookies-set returns Set-Cookie per entry
statement: The system shall emit one Set-Cookie header per k=v pair passed to /cookies/set.

title: Redirect count boundary
statement: The system shall accept /redirect/<n> with n in the range 1..30 inclusive and reject values above.

title: Basic-auth requires both segments
statement: The system shall route /basic-auth/<user>/<passwd> only when both user and passwd segments are provided.

title: Retrieve all players
statement: The system shall respond to GET /players with a JSON array of all players in the database.

title: Retrieve player by ID
statement: The system shall respond to GET /players/{playerId} with the corresponding player object.

title: Return 404 for unknown player ID
statement: The system shall return HTTP 404 when no player exists for the given ID on GET /players/{playerId}.

title: Retrieve player by squadNumber
statement: The system shall respond to GET /players/squadNumber/{squadNumber} with the player wearing that squad number.

title: Return 404 for unknown squadNumber
statement: The system shall return HTTP 404 when no player has the requested squad number.

title: Create new player
statement: The system shall create a player and respond with HTTP 201 when POST /players/ receives a valid Player payload.
expected_outcomes: Location header points to new resource

title: Reject duplicate playerId on create
statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 409 Conflict when POST /players/ is called with an ID that already exists.

title: Reject player with duplicate squadNumber
statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 409 Conflict when the squadNumber in a new player already belongs to another player.

title: Reject malformed player payload
statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity when POST /players/ receives a body that fails Player schema validation.

title: Update existing player
statement: The system shall replace an existing player when PUT /players/{playerId} is called with a valid body and matching ID.

title: PUT rejects payload ID mismatch
statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 400 when the playerId in the path does not match the id in the PUT body.

title: PUT rejects unknown player
statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 404 when PUT targets a playerId that does not exist.

title: PUT rejects squadNumber conflict
statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 409 when the updated squadNumber collides with another player's squadNumber.

title: Delete player
statement: The system shall delete the specified player and respond with HTTP 204 when DELETE /players/{playerId} is called.

title: DELETE rejects unknown player
statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 404 on DELETE for a non-existent playerId.

title: Health probe returns liveness
statement: The system shall respond to GET /health/ with HTTP 200 and a status:'ok' JSON body.

title: Emit OpenAPI schema
statement: The system shall serve an OpenAPI 3.x JSON specification at GET /openapi.json.

title: Emit Swagger UI
statement: The system shall serve interactive Swagger UI documentation at GET /docs.

title: Player creation persists to DB
statement: The system shall commit newly created players to the players table so subsequent GET requests return them.

title: Player update persists to DB
statement: The system shall write updates to the players table so subsequent GET calls reflect the modification.

title: Player deletion persists to DB
statement: The system shall remove the row from the players table so GET returns 404 afterwards.

title: Reject empty firstName
statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 422 when the Player payload contains an empty firstName.

title: Reject negative squadNumber
statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 422 when squadNumber is not a positive integer.

title: Reject invalid date-of-birth format
statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 422 when dateOfBirth cannot be parsed as ISO-8601 date.

title: Empty player list returns empty array
statement: The system shall respond to GET /players when the table is empty with HTTP 200 and an empty JSON array.
triggers: empty player list returns empty array

title: Content-Type is JSON
statement: The system shall return application/json Content-Type on all /players endpoints returning a body.

title: Location header on create
statement: The system shall set Location: /players/{new_id} on the 201 Created response.

title: Create schema on startup
statement: The system shall create the players table via SQLAlchemy metadata at application startup if it does not exist.

title: PUT is idempotent
statement: The system shall produce the same terminal state when PUT is repeated with an identical payload for the same playerId.

title: DELETE is idempotent
statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 404 on second and subsequent DELETE calls for the same playerId.

title: Return all players sorted by id
statement: The system shall list players in insertion (id) order on GET /players/.
triggers: return all players sorted by id

title: Player payload includes squadNumber
statement: The system shall include the squadNumber field on every response body under /players/.

title: Player payload includes firstName and lastName
statement: The system shall include firstName and lastName fields on every player response.
triggers: player payload includes firstname and lastname

title: Player payload includes position
statement: The system shall include the position field on every player response.

title: Reject player creation with invalid id type
statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 422 when POST /players/ receives an id that is not an integer.
triggers: reject player creation with invalid id type

title: Return 405 for unsupported /players root method
statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 405 when using DELETE on /players/ (collection).

title: Reject squadNumber lookup for non-numeric value
statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 422 when GET /players/squadNumber/{value} receives a non-integer segment.
triggers: reject squadnumber lookup for non-numeric value

title: PUT /players/{id} requires body
statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 422 when PUT /players/{playerId} is called without a request body.

title: Health responds under load-balancer probe path
statement: The system shall serve GET /health/ with sub-second latency and no external dependencies required.
triggers: health responds under load-balancer probe path

title: Player POST accepts nickname optionally
statement: The system shall accept POST /players/ payloads without a nickname field and treat nickname as optional.

title: Show index page
statement: The system shall respond to GET / with an HTML page listing all posts ordered by created descending.

title: Register form GET
statement: The system shall serve a registration form at GET /auth/register.

title: Register new user
statement: The system shall create a new user with a hashed password when POST /auth/register receives a unique username and non-empty password, then redirect to /auth/login.

title: Register requires username
statement: The system shall render the register form with an error message when POST /auth/register omits the username.

title: Register requires password
statement: The system shall render the register form with an error message when POST /auth/register omits the password.

title: Register rejects duplicate username
statement: The system shall render an error message when POST /auth/register is called with a username already present in the users table.

title: Login form GET
statement: The system shall serve a login form at GET /auth/login.

title: Login sets session on success
statement: The system shall set session['user_id'] and redirect to / when POST /auth/login receives a matching username and password.

title: Login rejects wrong username
statement: The system shall render an 'Incorrect username.' error when the supplied username is not found.

title: Login rejects wrong password
statement: The system shall render an 'Incorrect password.' error when the password hash comparison fails.

title: Logout clears session
statement: The system shall clear the session and redirect to / on GET /auth/logout.

title: Login required for create
statement: The system shall redirect anonymous users to /auth/login when they attempt GET /create.

title: Login required for update
statement: The system shall redirect anonymous users to /auth/login when they attempt GET /<id>/update.

title: Login required for delete
statement: The system shall redirect anonymous users to /auth/login when they POST /<id>/delete.

title: Create new post
statement: The system shall insert a new post attributed to the logged-in user when POST /create receives a title and body, then redirect to /.

title: Create requires title
statement: The system shall render 'Title is required.' when POST /create omits the title field.

title: Update existing post
statement: The system shall update the row when POST /<id>/update is called by the post's author with a title and body, and redirect to /.

title: Update requires title
statement: The system shall render 'Title is required.' when POST /<id>/update omits the title.

title: Update only by author
statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 403 Forbidden when a user attempts to update a post they did not author.

title: Delete only by author
statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 403 Forbidden when a user attempts to delete a post they did not author.

title: Delete post
statement: The system shall remove the post row and redirect to / when POST /<id>/delete is issued by the post's author.

title: Return 404 on unknown post
statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 404 when GET/POST /<id>/update or /<id>/delete references a non-existent post id.

title: Init-db CLI creates schema
statement: The system shall create the users and post tables when the flask init-db CLI command is invoked.

title: Posts include author username
statement: The system shall join post rows with users so index/detail responses include the author's username.

title: Reuse db connection per request
statement: The system shall reuse a single sqlite3 connection per Flask request via flask.g.

title: Close db connection after request
statement: The system shall close the sqlite3 connection at the end of every request via teardown_appcontext.

title: Register form html served
statement: The system shall include HTML input fields named 'username' and 'password' in the /auth/register page.

title: Session persists across requests
statement: The system shall keep session['user_id'] populated across requests until logout for authenticated users.

title: load_logged_in_user populates g.user
statement: The system shall populate flask.g.user with the User row for the authenticated session on every request.

title: POST-only actions reject GET
statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 405 when GET is used on /<id>/delete.

title: Config testing flag switches DB path
statement: The system shall use the TESTING configuration's DATABASE path when TESTING is set in create_app.
triggers: config testing flag switches db path

title: Index shows post author name
statement: The system shall render the author's username alongside each post on the index page.

title: Update pre-populates form
statement: The system shall pre-fill the update form with the existing post's title and body.

title: Sessions use secret key
statement: The system shall sign session cookies with the SECRET_KEY loaded from application config.

title: Password hashing uses generate_password_hash
statement: The system shall store passwords via werkzeug generate_password_hash rather than plaintext.

title: Login case-sensitive username
statement: The system shall treat usernames as case-sensitive on POST /auth/login.

title: Index renders even with zero posts
statement: The system shall render the index page with 'No posts' or empty state when the post table is empty.
triggers: index renders even with zero posts

title: Create form GET returns 200
statement: The system shall serve the create-post form at GET /create for authenticated users.

title: Update form GET returns 200 for author
statement: The system shall serve the update form at GET /<id>/update when the current user is the post's author.
triggers: update form get returns 200 for author

title: Blog post title required on update
statement: The system shall reject POST /<id>/update with a missing title, rendering an error.
triggers: blog post title required on update

title: Flaskr uses sqlite as backing store
statement: The system shall persist users and posts in a sqlite3 database file named flaskr.sqlite by default.
triggers: flaskr uses sqlite as backing store

title: Init-db closes existing connection
statement: The system shall close any open connection before recreating the schema during init-db.

title: Session cookie has HttpOnly attribute
statement: The system shall set HttpOnly on the session cookie.

title: Create task
statement: The system shall create a new task and respond with HTTP 201 and the created task body when POST /tasks/ receives a valid TaskCreate payload.
expected_outcomes: response body includes id, title, completed=false

title: Reject empty title on create
statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 422 when the title field of POST /tasks/ is missing.

title: Reject non-string title
statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 422 when the title field is not a string.

title: List all tasks
statement: The system shall respond to GET /tasks/ with a JSON array of all tasks, honouring optional skip and limit query parameters.

title: Pagination via skip and limit
statement: The system shall skip the first 'skip' items and cap the returned count at 'limit' when both are supplied to GET /tasks/.

title: Reject negative skip
statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 422 when the skip parameter is negative.

title: Reject limit above cap
statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 422 when the limit parameter exceeds the maximum allowed.

title: Retrieve task by id
statement: The system shall respond to GET /tasks/{task_id} with the corresponding task object.

title: 404 on unknown task id
statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 404 and detail 'Task not found' when the id does not exist.

title: Update task
statement: The system shall update mutable fields of the task and return the updated object when PUT /tasks/{task_id} is called with a valid body.

title: Update unknown returns 404
statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 404 when PUT targets a non-existent task id.

title: Partial update supported
statement: The system shall accept a partial payload on PUT /tasks/{task_id} and leave omitted fields unchanged.

title: Delete task
statement: The system shall delete the task and respond with a confirmation body when DELETE /tasks/{task_id} is called.

title: Delete unknown returns 404
statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 404 when DELETE targets a non-existent task id.

title: Mark task complete
statement: The system shall set completed=true when a PUT payload includes {"completed": true}.

title: Task has default completed=false
statement: The system shall default the completed field to false when POST /tasks/ omits it.

title: Task description optional
statement: The system shall accept POST /tasks/ payloads without a description field.

title: Root endpoint responds
statement: The system shall serve a welcome message at GET / with HTTP 200.

title: Emit OpenAPI schema
statement: The system shall serve an OpenAPI 3.x JSON specification at GET /openapi.json.

title: Emit Swagger UI
statement: The system shall serve interactive Swagger UI at GET /docs.

title: Task creation persists
statement: The system shall commit new task rows so subsequent GET calls return them across requests.

title: Task update persists
statement: The system shall persist PUT changes so subsequent GET requests reflect the update.

title: Task deletion persists
statement: The system shall remove deleted rows so subsequent GET returns 404 for that id.

title: Create schema on startup
statement: The system shall create the tasks table via SQLAlchemy metadata at application startup.

title: Return JSON content type
statement: The system shall return application/json Content-Type on all /tasks endpoints returning a body.

title: Unsupported methods rejected
statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 405 when using an unsupported method against /tasks/{task_id}.

title: PUT is idempotent
statement: The system shall produce the same terminal state when PUT is repeated with the same body for the same task_id.

title: DELETE is idempotent
statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 404 for subsequent DELETE calls on the same task_id.

title: Task title max length
statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 422 when the title exceeds the maximum length constraint.

title: Task id is auto-generated
statement: The system shall assign a unique integer id to each new task; client-supplied ids in the payload shall be ignored.

title: Task title accepts unicode
statement: The system shall accept task titles containing UTF-8 characters and return them intact.

title: Task description accepts long text
statement: The system shall accept task descriptions up to at least 1000 characters.

title: List returns empty array when db empty
statement: The system shall return an empty JSON array on GET /tasks/ when no tasks exist.
triggers: list returns empty array when db empty

title: Task ids are monotonically increasing
statement: The system shall assign strictly increasing integer ids to newly created tasks.

title: Deleting all tasks leaves empty table
statement: The system shall leave GET /tasks/ returning [] after every task has been deleted.
triggers: deleting all tasks leaves empty table

title: Fetching completed tasks
statement: The system shall optionally filter tasks by completed status when a filter query parameter is supplied.

title: Task title trimmed of whitespace
statement: The system shall trim leading and trailing whitespace from the title on POST /tasks/.

title: Task update rejects id changes
statement: The system shall ignore any id field in the PUT body and only mutate the task addressed by the URL.

title: Rate limit not enforced
statement: The system shall not throttle single-client request rates below 60/min.

title: OpenAPI includes task schemas
statement: The system shall document TaskCreate, TaskUpdate, and Task schemas in the OpenAPI spec.
